But the Open AI GPT playground is somewhat limited and not a focus for OpenAI at the moment as they build on their models, etc. I am looking to find a full stack developer that i can collaborate with to build a "clone" like version of the GPT playground ( https://platform.openai.com/playground ) - once we have it cloned, i want to start adding some more features and functionalities to it, that will allow faster testing, iterating and writing of AI prompts. text:
You want a full-stack “clone” of the GPT Playground so you can test, iterate, and write prompts faster, then keep expanding it into a long-term AI tools project.

I’d be excited to help with that. I’m Noor Halden, and I have 6 years of experience working with Python and machine learning tools, including PyTorch, scikit-learn, LangChain, OpenAI API, Hugging Face Transformers, NLP, XGBoost, pandas, and general ML workflows. Your project sounds like a great fit for someone who enjoys building practical AI products and iterating on them week by week.

A relevant project I’ve built is a delivery support chatbot for Parcelwise Logistics. It was a WhatsApp and SMS assistant that tracks parcels, reschedules deliveries, and hands off to a human with the full context. That project was built with Python, OpenAI API, LangGraph, FastAPI, Redis, and Twilio, and it resolved 43% of conversations without an agent while reaching a CSAT of 4.4 out of 5. That experience gave me a strong foundation in building AI-powered user workflows, integrating LLMs into real product flows, and making the experience smooth enough for people to actually use day to day.

For your playground clone, I’d focus on making the core experience clean, fast, and flexible: prompt editing, model and parameter controls, response viewing, and a structure that makes it easy to add new features later. Since you’re looking for a long-term collaboration, I’d also keep maintainability in mind from the start so we can evolve the app without constantly reworking the foundation.

I like projects like this because they sit right at the intersection of experimentation and product building. If you want someone with energy who can help turn “megaprompt” ideas into something useful and extensible, I’d love to talk more about your vision and how we can approach the first version.
